## Problem Statement

The operator wants a new Grok-backed coding conversation in the modded Codex harness displayed immediately to the right of the current conversation. Wake currently discovers exact tabs but can reject freshly resolved move previews as stale_target. That prevents dependable placement before real coding acceptance.

Issue #716 records this failure through CLI and MCP on installed Wake dev43, with no move applied. Dynamic titles and generation churn were observed; their causal relationship remains unproven. Closed #563 addressed related metadata sensitivity and #552 addressed formatting generation churn; neither establishes a fix for #716.

## Solution

Make ordinary exact-tab placement work through Wake's existing public controls. Discover the current and companion presentation attachments, preview placement immediately after the current tab, apply an authorized unchanged placement, and verify adjacency while preserving conversations and processes. Ordinary display updates must not fabricate replacement; genuine identity or conflicting layout changes must still hold safely.

This is a bounded correction to #716. Native Grok inference and real coding acceptance remain governed by #628. Reliable placement prepares that acceptance without restarting its design or claiming provider readiness.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want the current tab resolved by stable identity, so that its changing index cannot redirect placement.
2. As an operator, I want the companion tab resolved independently, so that similar titles cannot select another conversation.
3. As an operator, I want a new supported selected-profile tab available through existing creation controls, so that the intended coding harness is displayed.
4. As an operator, I want exact account, profile and build ownership retained, so that placement cannot substitute another environment.
5. As an operator, I want the companion immediately to the right of the current tab, so that I can inspect both coding workflows together.
6. As an operator, I want a read-only placement preview, so that I can inspect the intended effect before application.
7. As a CLI caller, I want ordinary fresh target resolution to work, so that I do not manufacture internal identity envelopes.
8. As an MCP caller, I want list-to-preview target handling to work, so that automation can use the documented public workflow.
9. As an operator, I want title changes tolerated during placement preparation, so that normal coding activity does not fabricate a stale target.
10. As an operator, I want irrelevant CWD, command and activity observations separated from identity, so that observation refresh does not prevent valid moves.
11. As an operator, I want changed process births and pane replacements rejected, so that an old intent cannot affect a replacement attachment.
12. As an operator, I want terminal namespace replacement rejected, so that a reused name cannot redirect the operation.
13. As an operator, I want conflicting manual layout changes detected, so that application cannot overwrite newer work.
14. As an operator, I want existing focus, pin and input protections respected, so that placement does not disrupt interaction.
15. As an operator, I want unrelated tabs and their relative order preserved, so that a local placement does not reorganize my environment.
16. As an operator, I want both conversations and pane/process identities preserved, so that moving a presentation attachment does not restart coding work.
17. As an operator, I want an already adjacent arrangement reported as a no-op, so that repeated inspection does not create new effects.
18. As an agent, I want a recoverable operation receipt, so that an uncertain response can be reconciled without replay.
19. As an operator, I want unsupported or protected placement explained precisely, so that I can distinguish a legitimate hold from the stale-target defect.
20. As an operator, I want installed-package qualification separated from source tests, so that evidence describes the controls I actually use.
21. As an operator, I want tab preparation to send no model requests, so that layout work does not consume provider allowance.
22. As an operator, I want real Grok coding acceptance reported separately, so that adjacency alone cannot close #628.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing tab discovery, lifecycle, controller operation journal, native tmux transport and selected-profile creation owners. Introduce no parallel tab registry, launcher or provider worker.
- Diagnose which target-generation fields cause #716 before selecting the correction. Existing source distinguishes observation targets from lifecycle targets; verify caller propagation and destination validation rather than assuming an owner-level defect.
- Preserve operation-specific identity and placement fences. Ignore a changing observation only where it is irrelevant to that operation; keep relevant ordering criteria and input custody protections exact.
- Resolve placement relative to the exact sibling from a fresh layout using existing supported operations. No new endpoint or relative-placement flag is prescribed by this specification.
- Preview freezes exact source, destination and sibling context. Apply revalidates relevant identities and layout, and readback verifies immediate adjacency and preserved bindings.
- Retain existing request identity, held/uncertain outcomes and reconciliation semantics. Do not turn an uncertain move into a fresh intent or automatically retry it.
- Support the evidenced Cooper POSIX Byobu/tmux path. Existing capability errors remain explicit for unsupported environments.
- Preserve original #716 reproduction details and uncertainty when publishing this specification as an update to that issue.

## Testing Decisions

- Operator-approved primary seam: installed public Wake tab controls, exercised through ordinary CLI and actual MCP calls against an owned disposable tmux server. Use one shared behavioral journey across those caller adapters.
- Exercise discovery, fresh resolution, preview, apply and readback while pane titles and other irrelevant observations change. Reproduce #716 before correction and demonstrate success afterward.
- Prove negative controls for process/pane/namespace replacement and conflicting manual moves. Verify adjacency, unchanged conversation bindings, pane/process births, focus, unrelated-tab order and protected-tab behavior.
- Exercise uncertain replies and retained request identity through the existing operation journal, proving reconciliation does not duplicate movement. Keep terminal input fencing distinct from lifecycle movement.
- Reuse existing real disposable-tmux lifecycle tests, ordinary CLI/MCP lifecycle caller tests, and installed public-transport acceptance patterns. Test externally visible results rather than hash construction or private helper shape.
- Use provider-free synthetic profile/conversation fixtures where bindings are required. Qualify the exact installed prefix/package and clean up only owned resources, with a final process/resource readback.
- Run applicable checks locally under the CI cost policy. Record commands, results, source commit, package identity and material environment differences; do not run paid hosted CI.
- Any later placement in the operator's real terminal session requires its own authorized exact-target execution and readback. It is not performed by spec publication or disposable qualification.

## Out of Scope

- Executing Grok inference, renewing expired live authority, replaying GR01, refreshing credentials or changing billing.
- Redesigning #628, reopening completed clock/package work, rebuilding native Codex without a new evidenced blocker, or claiming mixed-provider live acceptance.
- Broad automatic organization, cross-backend transfers, native Windows psmux qualification or unrelated tab-management defects.
- Weakening stale-identity checks, force-based ordinary placement, restarting existing agents, deleting conversations or moving unrelated production tabs.
- Implementation, merge, deployment or live layout mutation as part of publishing this specification.

## Further Notes

Canonical defect owner: #716. Native Grok acceptance owner: #628. Existing selected-profile tab creation: #515. Related historical metadata correction: #563. Keep source-qualified, integrated, installed and operational acceptance distinct.

Next bounded execution outcome after specification readiness: reproduce and repair the public fresh-target placement failure, qualify it with disposable native tabs, and report the exact installed/runtime gate remaining before the operator's adjacent Grok coding session.

## Original defect report (preserved)

*This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Defect: fresh tab targets repeatedly fail move preview

The operator requested an existing companion software tab immediately to the right of the current workspace tab. Codex Wake discovers both exact conversations and windows, but both local CLI and MCP move previews return `stale_target`, preventing placement. No move was applied.

## Observed environment and reproduction

- Installed CLI: `codex-wake 0.22.0.dev43`; source checkout observed at `1aa498674a4907f93b5216a4a98dd75a22c6ecec` (installed-source equivalence not established).
- Cooper, POSIX tmux; discovered workspace `tmux-7cbd633a-1`, label `default`.
- Companion window `@17`, index 14; originating window `@381`, index 16. Desired companion index: 17.
- `wake_tabs_list` succeeds and returns targets, exact window IDs and native conversation bindings.
- Local CLI: `codex-wake tabs move --workspace tmux-7cbd633a-1 --window @17 --destination default --index 17 --dry-run --json` returns an admitted operation with `phase: uncertain`, `reason: stale_target`, no result.
- Refreshing `wake_tabs_list`, then passing its exact target as both `expected_target` and `expected_destination` to `wake_tabs_move` with `preview:true` gives the same result. Request ID: `workbench-software-tab-right-preview-v1`.
- Workspace generation changed on successive observations despite no intentional layout mutation. Dynamic pane titles were visible. Whether title/activity metadata causes the generation churn is an inference, not established root cause.
- Looking up the CLI-generated operation ID with `tabs result --request-id` returned `operation_not_found`; that may reflect using an operation ID where an independently retained request ID was expected. Treat as diagnostic uncertainty, not a confirmed second defect.

## Expected outcome

A freshly resolved unchanged attachment should support move preview and authorized placement. Preserve exact session/window/pane process identity fences and newer human layout changes. Do not solve this by dropping stale-identity protection or requiring force for routine placement.

## Acceptance

1. Reproduce with transient pane titles/activity changing while attachment identity and layout remain stable; explain which generation fields invalidate the request.
2. Fresh CLI resolution and list-to-MCP target pins allow preview and move of the existing conversation immediately after a specified sibling.
3. Actual window/pane replacement and conflicting human layout changes still reject safely.
4. Post-move readback verifies adjacency and preservation of both conversation bindings; retain a recoverable operation receipt.

Related: #552 fixed similar generation churn for formatting only and explicitly excluded lifecycle/input pins; #506 implemented exact tab lifecycle operations. This report concerns move preview and does not establish that either prior fix regressed.

Priority suggestion: medium. State: triage. No implementation or deployment requested by this report.
